cohort_policy_note: The primary (2016-2024) cohort is the predetermined production policy. This report measures whether the combined-cohort or factor-only alternatives score better or worse; it does not select a policy from whichever alternative happens to score best on the same held-out observations, and a material deterioration here is a finding to review, not a reason to change the assertion in this note.

primary.role: production: the primary (2016-2024) cohort's own gust factor and profile fit

factor_only.wind_calibration_id: diagnostic: fl-asos-hurricane-peaks-v2 gust factor + fl-asos-hurricane-peaks-v2 profile
factor_only.role: diagnostic only: the combined cohort's gust factor with the primary cohort's decay and land factor frozen, to isolate arithmetic sensitivity to the gust factor alone. Not an independently fitted bundle; never a candidate production policy.

combined.role: alternative: the combined (2004-2024) cohort's own gust factor and profile fit, refit jointly

current_production.role: before-change benchmark: the production bundle as captured by the caller before this comparison's own fits were promoted (see the module docstring's current_production_bundle note).

primary.method: leave one storm out: refit the gust factor, decay and land factor on the other cohort storms, score the held-out storm with all three

combined.method: leave one storm out: refit the gust factor, decay and land factor on the other cohort storms, score the held-out storm with all three

holdout.note: Republished verbatim from each cohort's own leave-one-storm-out cross-validation (scripts/calibrate_wind_field.py) - not recomputed here, and not interchangeable with the fixed-bundle wind_accuracy comparison above, which scores one already-chosen bundle rather than refitting per fold. factor_only has no holdout: it is not an independently fitted bundle, so there is nothing to leave a storm out of.

policy_template.label: Illustrative Florida homeowners policy - 5% hurricane deductible
policy_template.source: StormShield_Finance_Data_v5.xlsx, sheet 'Sample Policy Summary', built from Fla. Stat. 627.701 and Citizens Property Insurance guidance.
policy_template.warning: ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY - not a declarations page and not policy wording. Citizens states real coverages, deductibles, limits and exclusions vary by policy. Finance must approve this scope before any number leaves the prototype.

deductible.note: Fla. Stat. 627.701 requires insurers to offer $500, 2%, 5% and 10% hurricane-deductible options. The workbook's 'Data Request - Policy Examples' sheet asks for ONE option so worked examples stay internally consistent, and advises against 10%; 5% is the option its 'Sample Policy Summary' sheet already works through ($400,000 Coverage A -> $20,000). The percentage is applied to the documented policy base (Coverage A), never to the damage amount.

out_of_scope_v1: Second-hurricane-same-calendar-year deductible (Fla. Stat. 627.701(5)(a): the greater of the unmet first deductible or the AOP deductible). This engine prices each storm independently and resets the deductible, so a chronological multi-storm year needs a future model.
AOP deductible for non-hurricane wind. Stored here because the statutory rule needs it; unused in v1.
Contents, loss of use, flood and storm surge, premium changes, reinsurance, claim expenses.
Recoverable depreciation withheld until repairs complete under RCV.

config_held_constant.note: The demo's seeded roof-shape assignment (scripts/assign_demo_roof_shapes.py), this curve_set_id, the policy template and eligible upgrades are held identical across every scenario above, so a payout difference between scenarios is attributable to the wind bundle alone.

payout_comparison.aggregation_note: Every *_usd figure is a SUM over properties, for one storm and one scenario, never an average and never summed across storms into an endpoint total: portfolio_baseline_payout_usd sums each property's baseline (no-upgrade) payout; each entry of portfolio_avoided_payout_usd_by_upgrade sums avoided_payout_usd only over the properties eligible for that upgrade. Per-property figures (peak_gust_mph, baseline_payout_usd, avoided_payout_usd_by_upgrade) are reported alongside these sums, never blended with them.
